title: When Agents Act on Web3: An Attack-Surface Survey of MCP, Skills, and Tool Calling
abstract: arXiv:2608.17275v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI agents increasingly act rather than merely read: across the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem, the share of deployed tools that modify external state has risen from 27% to 65% of tool use. When agents exercise this authority on public blockchains through MCP, skills, and tool calling, the consequences of an attack are governed by the blockchain execution layer rather than by conventional software assumptions. This survey argues that four properties of that layer (irreversibility, signing authority, continuous autonomy, and sequence-level composition) qualitatively change the threat model, turning the recoverable failures of generic agent security into a standing, irreversible loss. translated_title: 当智能体在Web3中行动：MCP、技能与工具调用的攻击面综述
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17275v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：AI智能体越来越多地采取行动而不仅仅阅读：在模型上下文协议（MCP）生态系统中，修改外部状态的部署工具使用比例已从27%上升至65%。当智能体通过MCP、技能和工具调用在公共区块链上行使这种权限时，攻击的后果由区块链执行层而非传统软件假设所决定。本综述认为，该层的四个属性（不可逆性、签名授权、持续自主性和序列级组合）从根本上改变了威胁模型，将通用智能体安全中的可恢复失败转变为持续性的、不可逆转的损失。我们将零散的MCP安全文献组织成一个攻击面分类体系，并贡献了一个Web3风险映射矩阵，该矩阵将每类攻击与其放大后的影响、负责的放大器、代表性缓解措施及残余风险联系起来。
tldr: 本文综述了AI智能体在Web3环境中通过MCP等工具行动时的攻击面，指出区块链的不可逆性等特性使安全威胁从可恢复失败变为持久损失，并提出了攻击分类和风险映射矩阵。
en_tdlr: This survey examines the attack surface of AI agents acting on Web3 via MCP and tools, arguing that blockchain's irreversibility transforms security failures into permanent losses, and provides an attack taxonomy and risk-mapping matrix.
